observation_period: 65th Congress (1917 to 1918) to the 119th Congress (2025 to 2026), through November 10, 2026, the date of the Senate’s latest roll call vote when the page was read
universe_or_base: Cloture motions filed, votes on cloture and cloture invoked, on legislation and nominations together
vintage: Page as read on November 12, 2026, every row; first read November 11, 2026, when the 119th Congress row was frozen as 294 motions, 294 votes and 247 invoked
qualification: Counts mix bills and nominations, and the vote needed changed over time (two-thirds of those voting until 1975, then three-fifths of senators for most matters; a simple majority for nominations since 2013 and 2017). The 119th Congress is still in session; its row counts votes through November 10, 2026

complete.description: false while the Congress is in session

printed_source_line: Source: United States Senate, Senate Action on Cloture Motions, 65th Congress (1917) to the 119th Congress through November 10, 2026, United States Senate. Retrieved November 12, 2026. Counts include bills and nominations; the votes needed changed in 1975, 2013 and 2017.
notes: The 2013 and 2017 changes, confirmed November 12, 2026 from the Senate’s own record: on November 21, 2013, Senator Reid raised "a point of order that the vote on cloture under rule XXII for all nominations other than for the Supreme Court of the United States is by majority vote" (Congressional Record, Senate, November 21, 2013); the Senate voted 48 to 52 not to sustain the chair’s ruling against it (vote 242), and then invoked cloture on Patricia Ann Millett’s nomination 55 to 43 with a majority requirement of one-half (vote 244). On April 6, 2017, the Senate voted 48 to 52 not to sustain the chair (vote 109) and invoked cloture on Neil M. Gorsuch’s Supreme Court nomination 55 to 45 with a majority requirement of one-half (vote 110). Sources: https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CREC-2013-11-21/pdf/CREC-2013-11-21-senate.pdf ; https://www.senate.gov/legislative/LIS/roll_call_votes/vote1131/vote_113_1_00242.xml (and 00244) ; https://www.senate.gov/legislative/LIS/roll_call_votes/vote1151/vote_115_1_00109.xml (and 00110).

The 119th Congress row, corrected November 12, 2026 (statistics review M3). The page read that day gives the 119th Congress 297 motions filed, 295 votes on cloture and 248 times invoked, and every other row equals the file. The Senate’s own vote lists give the same 295 and 248: 289 votes whose question names cloture in vote_menu_119_1.xml and vote_menu_119_2.xml, plus 6 the lists show with no question, each read from its own record as "On the Cloture Motion" (session and vote: 1-653 cloture motion agreed to, 1-546 cloture motion agreed to, 1-525 cloture motion agreed to, 1-522 cloture motion rejected, 2-221 cloture motion agreed to, 2-124 cloture motion agreed to). The latest roll call vote was number 258 of the second session, November 10, 2026. The row frozen November 11 (294, 294 and 247) matched neither; the round 0 download is gone, so the cause was not found. Motions filed come from the page only; the vote lists do not record a motion until it is voted on.

On September 17, 2025, cloture on a group of nominations considered together failed 51 to 48 under a three-fifths requirement (vote 522 of the first session); the Senate then voted 47 to 52 not to sustain the chair (vote 524) and invoked cloture on the same group 52 to 47 with a majority requirement of one-half (vote 525). Read from each vote’s record on senate.gov, November 12, 2026. A chart that names the changes in the votes needed may add this one.
